accepted.question_text: Does the nonlinear Schrodinger equation posed on a tree graph admit a rigorous well-posedness theory comparable to the star-graph case, beyond the currently available partial results based on dispersive estimates?

evidence.quote: By the way a result of well posedness of NLS on trees in not yet proven, although well plausible; a step in this direction with proof of relevant dispersive estimates is given in [26, 27].

accepted.question_text: When a nonlinear Schrodinger equation is posed on a system of thin tubes or guides connected at junctions and the transversal tube size shrinks to zero, does the limiting dynamics converge to an NLS on a metric graph, and if so which vertex boundary conditions appear in the limit? How do those limiting boundary conditions depend on the specific shrinking procedure for the tubes, guides, and junction size, and on whether the thin-tube boundary condition is Neumann or Dirichlet?

evidence.quote: A first problem is getting the limit of a certain dynamical model, e.g. NLS equation defined on the system of thin guides when transversal size of tube vanishes. It is reasonable to conjecture that this limit should be a NLS on a graph as defined before, but with which boundary conditions? And how the boundary conditions at the vertex could depend on the limit process of shrinking the tubes, guides and junction size?
A further difficulty could be the dependence of limit process on the conditions at the boundary of the thin tube, e.g. Neumann or Dirichlet.
They remain open for nonlinear models, where there is no literature

accepted.question_text: Can one rigorously derive a quasi-one-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii or nonlinear Schrodinger equation on a graph-like structure such as a Y-junction from a many-body Bose-Einstein-condensate model, for example by starting from an N-body theory on the graph and taking the N to infinity limit with suitable scalings, while correctly determining the vertex boundary condition in the limit? The boundary-condition issue is already open even for the simplest graph with two edges, namely a line with a defect.

evidence.quote: Being confident that a Gross-Pitaevskii equation realizes the correct quasi one dimensional limit, a similar procedure could be attempted on graphlike structure, for example on a Y-junction; to simplify the analysis, one could start directly from a N-body theory on the graph, and to attempt at taking the N → ∞ limit with suitable scalings.
Notice that the main problem, i.e. the treatment of the boundary condition, it is open also in the simplest case of a graph with two edges, i.e. a line with a defect.

accepted.question_text: For focusing NLS on a star graph with a delta interaction at the vertex, if the threshold condition that guarantees an absolute constrained minimum of the reduced action fails, does the action still have a local minimum on the Nehari manifold that lies above the infimum? Is there an analogous local constrained minimum for the energy functional when the mass falls outside the regime where a ground state exists?

evidence.quote: It is a conjecture that the action has a local constrained minimum that is larger than the infimum when the condition −N sqrt(omega) < alpha < alpha* fails, and similarly for the constrained energy with a corresponding condition on mass.

accepted.question_text: On graphs more complicated than a star graph, such as trees or graphs with loops, can one build an orbital-stability or orbital-instability theory for nonlinear standing waves of the nonlinear Schrodinger equation when explicit formulas for the standing waves are unavailable? In particular, can one effectively count negative eigenvalues of the linearized operator and verify the Vakhitov-Kolokolov condition in these less explicit graph geometries?

evidence.quote: One could ask if a similar analysis could be performed on more complex graphs, for example trees or graphs with loops.

The first is that a direct analysis of the conditions guaranteeing orbital stability or instability of standing waves, in particular counting of negative eigenvalues of L1 and verification of Vakhitov-Kolokolov condition, becomes in general impossible or at least very difficult.

accepted.question_text: For nonlinear Schrodinger equations on nontrivial graphs, how can one construct and identify branches of nonlinear stationary or bound states that do not bifurcate from any linear eigenstate? The paper notes that standard bifurcation theory can produce branches with a linear counterpart near the linear ground state, but it leaves open how to obtain excited states or other bound states without a linear counterpart.

evidence.quote: But there are several problems which arise at this point.

A second problem is that bifurcation theory allows to identify branches of nonlinear stationary states which have a linear counterpart, but how to obtain branches of states without linear counterpart, which exist as we know from the example of nonlinear excited states in star graphs?

accepted.question_text: Are standing waves of the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on graphs asymptotically stable in the following sense: every solution that starts near a standing wave in the energy norm eventually decomposes into a possibly different nearby standing wave, a dispersive term evolving under the linear graph Hamiltonian, and a remainder that decays to zero in L2 as time goes to infinity? More concretely, can one control the spectrum and time evolution of the non-selfadjoint linearized Hamiltonian J L on graphs, together with the decay of nonlinear remainders, well enough to prove such relaxation?
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotic stability of graph standing waves

evidence.quote: A final open and difficult problem is the so called asymptotic stability of standing waves.
In our case a standing wave Phi_omega e^{i omega t} is said asymptotically stable if for every solution u(t) starting near Phi_omega in the energy norm, one has the representation
The problem is very hard and there is only partial information also in the case of a NLS equation on the line with a delta potential (see [51]).

Part of the difficulties are due to the fact that the Hamiltonian structure plays a role in the analysis and this makes unavoidable to study the spectrum of the not selfadjoint and not skew adjoint operator J L (the Hamiltonian linearization) and to get dispersive estimates about its evolution exp(tJ L)

accepted.question_text: For the scattering of fast solitons in the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on star graphs, do multisoliton solutions exist, and what is the dynamical outcome when several solitons collide at the same vertex?

evidence.quote: Nothing it is presently known about the possible existence of multisolitons, or about the collision of several solitons at the vertex.

accepted.question_text: Can one develop a rigorous theory of soliton scattering for the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on graphs with nontrivial topology, especially trees, beyond the already treated star-graph and similar simple cases? In particular, how do network topology and the availability of Strichartz estimates affect the propagation and scattering of solitons on such graphs?

evidence.quote: On the contrary, scattering of solitons on graphs having a less trivial topology is an open problem. In particular it could be interesting the study of propagation of solitons on trees
Notice that among the main technical ingredients are Strichartz estimates, and every generalization needs their validity.

accepted.question_text: After a soliton scatters at a graph vertex, can the time interval on which the outgoing waves are accurately approximated by solitary waves be extended beyond the logarithmic-in-velocity scale proved in the paper? How does that longer-timescale question depend on the initial data and on the external potential?
accepted.context_brief: Longer validity timescale for outgoing solitons

evidence.quote: Another important problem concerns the possibility of extending the timescale of validity of approximation by the solitary outgoing waves.

in [54], some considerations are given about the possibility of longer timescales of outgoing soliton approximation depending on the initial data and external potential, but it is unclear whether similar considerations can be applied to the present case.

accepted.question_text: For nonlinear Schrodinger equations on graphs whose nonlinearity is close to the integrable cubic case but not exactly cubic, are the outgoing waves produced by vertex scattering still close to solitons over timescales comparable to those proved in the integrable cubic setting?

evidence.quote: As regards the limitation to cubic NLS, the fundamental asymptotics proved in [52] and used to get the analogous result on graphs depend on the integrability of cubic NLS.
One can conjecture that for nonlinearities close to integrable the outgoing waves are close to solitons over timescale similar to the above ones.

accepted.question_text: What rigorous mechanisms describe the capture of solitons by graph defects or junctions and the generation of new solitons in the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on graphs, particularly in dynamical regimes that are neither close to a standing wave nor in the fast-soliton scattering regime?

evidence.quote: In particular capture and generation of solitons are not yet understood from a rigorous point of view, and they represent a challenge to mathematical methods and theoretical interpretation where perhaps the simple but non trivial model of NLS equation on graphs could offer some insight.
